characterList.description: A middle-aged man with short grey hair and a beard. He wears a flat cap, a black puffer jacket and a grey backpack.
characterList.name: Hiker

content_metadata.description: Join a passionate hiker as he explores Dungeon Wood, discussing the advantages of tarp shelters over traditional tents, and delving into the wood's intriguing history. The journey features engaging narratives and scenic backdrops, setting the stage for future adventures.

qAndA.answer: He used a tent on a previous trip to Black Hill, where he encountered very cold temperatures.
qAndA.question: What type of shelter does the hiker say he used on a previous wild camping trip?

qAndA.answer: He plans to use the Rab Ridge Raider bivvy bag.
qAndA.question: What is the name of the bivvy bag the hiker plans to use for his new challenge?

qAndA.answer: He chose the Coyote color for his DD tarp.
qAndA.question: What color is the DD tarp the hiker purchased?

qAndA.answer: The battery on his GoPro died, and he was unable to remove the media mod due to overtightening the screws. He then switched to a different, unnamed camera.
qAndA.question: Why does the hiker suddenly switch from recording with his GoPro to another camera?

qAndA.answer: He mentions the Luddites hiding pistols in the wood after an uprising in 1812. These pistols were later used in the assassination of William Horsfall.
qAndA.question: What kind of historical event does the hiker mention happening in Dungeon Wood?

So I just want to let you know that after doing the West Highland Way Back in September 2021 I have really got the bug for wild camping and hiking.

For this new challenge I am going to need a much lighter backpack
I already own a Rab Ridge Raider bivvy bag

In 1812, the Luddites who shot William Horsfall fled through the wood from Crosland Moor, and according to some reports, two of their pistols were buried there
Shortly before the outbreak of the Second World War, the firm of David Brown had begun production of tractors at Meltham Mills. During the war, the company also manufactured vital aircraft gears. Whilst other gear factories at Coventry and Derby were repeatedly bombed by the Luftwaffe, the David Brown works at Lockwood and Meltham Mills were never targeted.
Following the end of the war, David Brown's soon became the primary user of the branch line.
